text:
mohit: Heads up — for the last 40m we've seen a heavy concentration of Pending GPU pods in us-west1-b. Scheduler shows Unschedulable due to 'Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'. Looks like a zone-level capacity blackhole, not our autoscaler failing to spin up (it tried).

elaine: Seen it too. Lots of jobs targeting nodepool 'gpu-ephemeral-usw1b' and the cloud API returns 0 available GPUs in the zone. Requests are bursty from batch-rerank and long-tail evals.

liam: Confirmed from k8s events on a stuck pod: `0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.` Tried to force new node group but cloud quotas for that zone are exhausted.

sasha: Can we stitch traffic to another region/cluster instead of waiting for quota? The Dedicated pools in us-west2 have idle capacity but cross-cluster routing is not wired for those job labels.

mohit: Agreed. Proposal: add a lightweight "stitch proxy" that rewrites nodeSelector/region label at admission for non-latency-sensitive queues, then route to us-west2-dedicated pools. That avoids full failover. Thoughts on security/data locality?

elaine: We should restrict to non-customer-sensitive workloads only. Also add a TTL on the stitch so jobs don't get sent 1000+ miles away indefinitely. Cost note: us-west2-dedicated is on reserved capacity so unit cost is better than on-demand us-west1.

liam: Quick CA/cluster-autoscaler config snippet we could toggle (suggestion):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cluster-autoscaler-params
data:
  scale-down-enabled: "true"
  skip-nodes-with-local-storage: "false"
  expander: least-waste
  max-total-unready-percentage: "50"
```
We can also set per-node-group priorities to prefer pulling from regional-dedicated pools.

ops-bot: deploy-check: cross-cluster-stitcher v0.1 gate OK if ops-approved and e2e for label-rewrite passes.

sasha: Implementation detail — admission controller + mutating webhook can rewrite tolerations/affinity only for pods with label `gpu-fallback: allowed`. Keep default deny. Add audit log.

mohit: Also need circuit-breaker: if network latency or egress costs exceed threshold, rollback automatically. We'll capture metrics: job-latency, egress-bytes, token-cost-est.

elaine: From cost perspective: rough calc — moving 100k GPU-seconds to us-west2 deducts ~15% on per-token infra cost vs spinning up on-demand gpus in west1. But inter-region egress will add ~10% so net ~5% savings if jobs are tolerant.

liam: For immediate mitigation, I'm going to manually patch a small batch of low-priority pods to `nodeSelector: region=us-west2` and watch for failures. If that works, we'll flip the admission toggle.

mohit: Action items:
- liam: run manual patch + report by +30m (watch job latency).
- sasha: PR for mutating webhook + simple policy (allow list) by EOD.
- elaine: update runbook with decision tree (blackhole -> stitch -> fallback -> escalate) and cost comparison.
- infra-bot: open ticket against cloud quotas for us-west1 with priority P2.

infra-bot: ticket created: CLOUD-9853 "us-west1 GPU quota spike". Assigned to cloud-quotas.

sasha: Will also add a PromQL alert for zone GPU saturation: `sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="nvidia.com/gpu",zone=~"us-west1.*"}) - sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="nvidia.com/gpu",zone=~"us-west1.*"}) < 2` -> page.

mohit: Thanks all. If stitch approach looks stable we'll schedule a controlled rollout and a small canary for model evals only. :thumbsup:

liam: Patch applied to 10 pods, 9 drained/recreated in us-west2 successfully, 1 failed permission denied (configmap mount). Investigating.

elaine: Keep an eye on billing dashboards and the per-route latency graphs in console. I'll update runbook once we confirm metrics.

mohit: Great. We'll leave the thread open until quotas clear or stitch is live.
